name: Tanah Rata
tagline: The main town, guesthouses and the trailheads
description: The Cameron Highlands' principal settlement, a single main street of restaurants, guesthouses, banks and a small market, with several of the jungle trails starting within walking distance of it. It has the best connectivity and the only real concentration of services in the highlands.
bestFor: Anyone who needs services, buses and the trailheads within walking distance
pros: The best connectivity and services in the highlands
Several jungle trails start at the edge of town
Bus connections to Kuala Lumpur, Ipoh and Penang
cons: Busy with tour groups and weekend visitors

name: Brinchang
tagline: The night market town, five kilometres north
description: The second town, larger and less appealing than Tanah Rata, with hotel blocks, the weekend night market and the road up towards the tea estates and the mossy forest. It has more accommodation and lower prices, and the strawberry farms that Malaysian visitors come for.
bestFor: Cheaper stays with the night market and the estate road close
pros: The weekend night market and strawberry farms
On the road to the tea estates and Gunung Brinchang

name: Boh Tea Estate and Habu
tagline: Out among the terraces, where the tea actually grows
description: The estate roads east of the main valley, where the tea terraces roll over the hillsides and the Boh plantation runs a tea house on a ridge above them. Accommodation is a handful of estate bungalows and homestays, isolated and quiet, with mist most mornings.
bestFor: Stays that want the terraces out of the window and nothing else
pros: The tea terraces and the estate tea house
Genuinely quiet with mist and birdsong
The most striking setting in the highlands
cons: Twenty to thirty minutes to any shop

name: Ringlet
tagline: The lower town on the approach road, cheapest and warmest
description: The first settlement on the road up from the lowlands, lower and warmer than Tanah Rata, built around the reservoir and the vegetable farms that supply much of Malaysia. It is a working agricultural town with no tourism at all and by far the lowest prices in the highlands.
bestFor: Long stays at the lowest cost, in a town that has nothing to do with tourism
pros: The lowest rents and prices in the highlands
A genuine working town rather than a resort
cons: Twenty minutes up to Tanah Rata
Nothing to do and few restaurants
Less of the cool weather people come for

name: Gunung Brinchang and the Mossy Forest
tagline: The highest road in peninsular Malaysia, in the cloud
description: The summit road climbing to over 2,000m past the mossy forest, a rare cloud-forest ecosystem of stunted trees hung with moss and pitcher plants, reached by a boardwalk. There is essentially no accommodation up here, but it is the reason the highlands are ecologically significant.
bestFor: Day trips rather than a base, for the mossy forest and the summit view
pros: The mossy forest boardwalk and the summit tower
cons: A narrow, steep road with heavy tour traffic
In cloud most of the time
